key_insight: This work formulates and compares two PINN-based approaches for PDE-constrained optimal control—one that enforces the state constraint directly and one that enforces first-order optimality (state + adjoint) indirectly—clarifying trade-offs in formulation, training, and enforcement of optimality for semilinear parabolic PDEs.
problem_solved: Bridges classical PDE-constrained optimal control and physics-informed neural networks by providing principled PINN formulations to compute optimal controls for semilinear parabolic equations while handling state constraints and optimality conditions within a neural PDE solver framework.
method: Direct PINN: construct a single neural network (or coupled networks) and minimize the control objective with penalized PDE state residuals and boundary/initial conditions as constraints in the loss.

Indirect PINN: derive the first-order optimality system (state, adjoint, and control optimality condition) and train PINNs to satisfy the coupled optimality PDEs simultaneously, embedding adjoint information explicitly.

Case study: specialize the framework to a class of semilinear parabolic PDEs, derive the corresponding state/adjoint equations, and use collocation-based losses (PDE residuals, boundary/initial losses, control cost) to train the networks.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a clear roadmap to apply PINNs for PDE-constrained control, highlighting when to use direct vs indirect formulations and how to encode optimality information into neural solvers—useful for physics-based control, inverse problems, and scientific ML.

paper_title: PINNs in PDE Constrained Optimal Control Problems: Direct vs Indirect Methods
paper_authors: Zhen Zhang, Shanqing Liu, Alessandro Alla, Jerome Darbon, George Em Karniadakis
